jobs.title: Associate Vice President, Small Business Banking, Data and Analytics, Insights & Artificial Intelligence
jobs.description:
Work Location:

Toronto, Ontario, Canada

Hours

37.5

Line Of Business

Data & Analytics

Pay Details

$160,000 - $220,000 CAD

TD is committed to providing fair and equitable compensation opportunities to all colleagues. Growth opportunities and skill development are defining features of the colleague experience at TD. Our compensation policies and practices have been designed to allow colleagues to progress through the salary range over time as they progress in their role. The base pay actually offered may vary based upon the candidate's skills and experience, job-related knowledge, geographic location, and other specific business and organizational needs.

As a candidate, you are encouraged to ask compensation related questions and have an open dialogue with your recruiter who can provide you more specific details for this role.

Job Description

The Analytics, Insights and Artificial Intelligence function at TD is at the forefront of driving data-driven decision-making and innovation across the organization. It harnesses advanced analytics, AI, and machine learning to deliver actionable insights and enhance performance, while fostering innovation and competitive advantage. In this role, you will be supporting one of the businesses within TD's Canadian Personal and Small Business Banking segment.

Key Responsibilities

Act as a strategic partner to businesses in achieving critical business outcomes through the delivery of data-driven insights, analytics and AI solutions
Own the data, analytics and AI portfolio, translating priorities into a clear roadmap and influencing business strategy and investment decisions
Build and scale a best-in-class AI and agentic ecosystem, driving reusable, high-impact solutions across the organization
Architect and evolve a high-performing operating model enabling rapid, scalable delivery
Lead and develop a large team, building differentiated analytics and AI capabilities
Modernize and simplify the business intelligence ecosystem to unlock speed and insight
Build a top-tier, inclusive talent bench fostering innovation and accountability
Ensure strong governance, risk discipline, and regulatory alignment

Qualifications

10+ years of progressive leadership experience in analytics, AI, or data-driven strategy and solution delivery
Experience driving and delivering analytics and AI solutions in Big Tech, Fintech, financial services, or consulting
Experience with bringing to market practical Gen AI and agentic solutions with practical know-how of AI Tech/tooling and governance frameworks
Demonstrated success operating at senior executive levels and influencing strategy
Proven ability to build and scale high-performing teams
Advanced degree in a quantitative discipline (data science, engineering, mathematics, business, or finance) preferred

Key Skills & Capabilities

Commercial acumen and outcome-oriented thinking
Strong thought leadership with a bias for bold and transformative thinking
High degree of curiosity around business, Tech, and AI
Effectively communicate and influence wide range of leaders across business, Tech, and governance functions and multiple levels of leadership
Ability to navigate ambiguity and complexity
Can build strong team culture and lead by example

Who We Are

TD is one of the world's leading global financial institutions and is the fifth largest bank in North America by branches/stores. Every day, we strive to make every interaction, product, and experience remarkably human and refreshingly simple for over 27 million households and businesses in Canada, the United States and around the world. More than 95,000 TD colleagues bring their skills, talent, and creativity to foster deeper relationships, ensure disciplined execution, and build a simpler, faster banking experience. TD is deeply committed to being a leader in client experience, that is why we believe that all colleagues, no matter where they work, are client facing. Together, we are reimagining what banking can be for our clients, colleagues and communities.

Our Total Rewards Package

Our Total Rewards package reflects the investments we make in our colleagues to help them and their families achieve their financial, physical, and mental well-being goals. Total Rewards at TD includes a base salary, variable compensation, and several other key plans such as health and well-being benefits, savings and retirement programs, paid time off, banking benefits and discounts, career development, and reward and recognition programs. Learn more

Additional Information

We’re delighted that you’re considering building a career with TD. Through regular development conversations, training programs, and a competitive benefits plan, we’re committed to providing the support our colleagues need to thrive both at work and at home.

Please be advised that this job opportunity is subject to provincial regulation for employment purposes. It is imperative to acknowledge that each province or territory within the jurisdiction of Canada may have its own set of regulations, requirements.

Colleague Development

If you’re interested in a specific career path or are looking to build certain skills, we want to help you succeed. You’ll have regular career, development, and performance conversations with your manager, as well as access to an online learning platform and a variety of mentoring programs to help you unlock future opportunities.

If you’re passionate about helping clients and building deep, lasting relationships, TD offers diverse career paths where you can grow your expertise and make a meaningful impact.

We're committed to your success and foster a respectful workplace where diverse perspectives are valued, everyone has fair opportunities to grow, and you can unlock your full potential to achieve your career goals. Here at TD, we hire and develop the best.

Training & Onboarding

We will provide training and onboarding sessions to ensure that you’ve got everything you need to succeed in your new role.

Interview Process

We’ll reach out to candidates of interest to schedule an interview. We do our best to communicate outcomes to all applicants by email or phone call.

Accommodation

We look forward to hearing from you!

jobs.title: Director, International Business Transformation & Strategy Execution (flexible location)
jobs.description:
At ABB, we help industries run leaner and cleaner—and every person here makes that happen. You’ll be empowered to lead, supported to grow, and proud of the impact we create together. Join us and help run what runs the world.

The work model for the role is:
Hybrid

Your Role And Responsibilities

This Director role is a strategic transformation position within ABB's NEMA International division, reporting to the EVP International Sales. The role is pivotal in building a scalable international business platform by strengthening alignment across Regions, Business Lines and functions, removing structural barriers to growth and driving implementation of the Stabilize-Optimize-Scale roadmap. The successful candidate will drive business transformation across regions while building scalable operating foundations, combining expertise in strategy execution, operating-model redesign, business process management, change leadership, and executive influence within a complex global matrix.

The work model for the role is: hybrid ;

The role is contributing to the Motion NEMA Motors division globally.

International travel of approximately 30-40% will be required for the role.

You will be mainly accountable for:

Own and drive the NEMA International transformation roadmap aligned with the Stabilize-Optimize-Scale journey, translating strategy into prioritized initiatives with clear outcomes, milestones and success measures while maintaining visibility of progress and risks to leadership.
Act as senior integrator between NEMA International and Global Business Lines, establishing governance mechanisms and cross-functional commitments that align product, portfolio, and investment priorities with international market requirements while escalating critical dependencies that constrain growth.
Lead resolution of systemic barriers at the interfaces between International Sales, Global Operations, IT, Finance, HR and other supporting functions, converting fragmented issues into prioritized root-cause initiatives with clear accountability and measurable outcomes.
Serve as custodian of the NEMA International target operating model, ensuring organizational accountabilities, governance, processes, technology and capabilities evolve coherently to enable profitable international growth, from stabilization through optimization and scale, while designing the organization for future growth and acquisitions.
Lead an executive-level International Transformation Office that manages the transformation portfolio, governance cadence, dependency view and risk escalation, mobilizing cross-functional workstreams and intervening to resolve ownership gaps, resource constraints or delayed decisions.
Lead adoption of the new international organization and ways of working through change leadership, stakeholder engagement and capability building, while establishing a continuous improvement framework that connects frontline issues to structural business improvements and embeds continuous improvement into leadership accountability.

Qualifications for the role:

Minimum 10 years of progressive experience in business transformation, strategy execution, operating-model design, commercial excellence, enterprise program leadership or management consulting.
Bachelor's or Master's degree in Business Administration, Engineering, Strategy, Operations, Information Systems or a related discipline.
Experience in an internal strategy, transformation, business excellence or consulting role.
Demonstrated experience leading complex, cross-functional transformation across multiple geographies or business units.
Proven ability to align senior stakeholders and functions behind a shared agenda without relying on direct authority.
Experience translating strategy into executable roadmaps, governance, operating mechanisms and measurable outcomes.
Strong business acumen and ability to connect transformation to customer value, growth, margin, cash, productivity and organizational capability.
Excellent executive communication, facilitation and synthesis skills.
Ability to constructively challenge established practices and navigate ambiguity with pace and judgement.
Familiarity with international commercial models, CRM/ERP environments and end-to-end customer processes.
Experience in an industrial, manufacturing, electromechanical or B2B technology environment is an advantage. Recognized transformation, change management, Lean, Six Sigma or program-management certification is a plus.
Fluent English language skills.

More about us:

ABB’s NEMA Motors Division is a marketer, designer and manufacturer that offers Baldor-Reliance® industrial electric motors, primarily in North America. The Division focuses on quality, reliability and efficiency to provide a comprehensive offering of NEMA motors in the market across most industrial segments and applications.

We value people from different backgrounds. Apply today for your next career step within ABB and visit www.abb.com to learn about the impact of our solutions across the globe. #MyABBStory

We look forward to receiving your application (documents submitted in English are appreciated). If you want to discover more about ABB, take another look at our website
www.abb.com
.

_________________

Directeur(-trice) transformation des activités internationales et exécution de la stratégie (lieu de travail flexible)

Nos convictions

Chez ABB, nous nous engageons à relever les défis mondiaux. Nos valeurs fondamentales — la bienveillance, le courage, la curiosité et la collaboration —combinées à notre engagement envers la diversité, l’inclusion et l’égalité des chances, sont au cœur de notre volonté de donner à chacun et chacune les moyens de créer des solutions durables.

Écrivez le prochain chapitre de votre histoire chez ABB.

Votre rôle et vos responsabilités

Ce poste de direction est axé sur la transformation stratégique au sein de la division NEMA International d’ABB et relève du vice-président exécutif, ventes internationales. Il joue un rôle essentiel dans la mise en place d’une plateforme d’affaires internationales évolutive en renforçant l’alignement entre les régions, les secteurs d’activité et les fonctions, en éliminant les obstacles structurels à la croissance et en pilotant la mise en œuvre de la feuille de route Stabiliser-Optimiser-Déployer à grande échelle. La personne retenue pilotera la transformation des activités dans les différentes régions tout en établissant des fondations opérationnelles évolutives, en mettant à profit son expertise en exécution de la stratégie, en refonte des modèles opérationnels, en gestion des processus d’affaires, en leadership du changement et en influence auprès de la haute direction dans une structure matricielle mondiale complexe.

Le mode de travail pour ce poste est : hybride;

Ce poste contribue aux activités de la division Moteurs NEMA du secteur Motion à l’échelle mondiale.

Ce poste exige des déplacements internationaux représentant environ 30 à 40 % du temps de travail.

Vos principales responsabilités seront les suivantes :

Prendre en charge et piloter la feuille de route de transformation de NEMA International, en cohérence avec le parcours Stabiliser-Optimiser-Déployer à grande échelle, en traduisant la stratégie en initiatives prioritaires assorties de résultats, de jalons et de critères de réussite clairs, tout en assurant à la direction une visibilité sur les progrès et les risques.
Agir comme principal point d’intégration entre NEMA International et les secteurs d’activité mondiaux, en établissant des mécanismes de gouvernance et des engagements interfonctionnels qui alignent les priorités en matière de produits, de portefeuille et d’investissements sur les exigences des marchés internationaux, tout en portant à l’attention de la direction les interdépendances critiques qui freinent la croissance.
Piloter la résolution des obstacles systémiques aux interfaces entre les ventes internationales, les opérations mondiales, les TI, les finances, les RH et les autres fonctions de soutien, en regroupant les problèmes isolés en initiatives prioritaires visant leurs causes fondamentales, assorties de responsabilités claires et de résultats mesurables.
Veiller au maintien du modèle opérationnel cible de NEMA International, en s’assurant que les responsabilités organisationnelles, la gouvernance, les processus, les technologies et les capacités évoluent de façon cohérente pour soutenir une croissance internationale rentable, de la stabilisation à l’optimisation, puis au déploiement à grande échelle, tout en concevant l’organisation en fonction de sa croissance et de ses acquisitions futures.
Diriger un bureau de transformation internationale au niveau de la haute direction, responsable du portefeuille de transformation, du rythme de gouvernance, du suivi des interdépendances et du signalement des risques, en mobilisant les chantiers interfonctionnels et en intervenant pour résoudre les lacunes dans l’attribution des responsabilités, les contraintes de ressources ou les retards décisionnels.
Piloter l’adoption de la nouvelle organisation internationale et des nouvelles façons de travailler grâce au leadership du changement, à la mobilisation des parties prenantes et au développement des capacités, tout en établissant un cadre d’amélioration continue qui relie les problèmes de première ligne aux améliorations structurelles des activités et intègre l’amélioration continue aux responsabilités de la direction.

Qualifications Requises Pour Le Poste

Au moins 10 ans d’expérience avec des responsabilités croissantes en transformation des activités, en exécution de la stratégie, en conception de modèles opérationnels, en excellence commerciale, en direction de programmes d’entreprise ou en conseil en gestion.
Baccalauréat ou maîtrise en administration des affaires, en génie, en stratégie, en gestion des opérations, en systèmes d’information ou dans une discipline connexe.
Expérience dans un rôle interne en stratégie, en transformation, en excellence opérationnelle ou en consultation.
Expérience démontrée dans la direction de transformations complexes et interfonctionnelles touchant plusieurs régions géographiques ou unités d’affaires.
Capacité éprouvée à rallier les parties prenantes de la haute direction et les fonctions autour de priorités communes, sans s’appuyer sur une autorité hiérarchique directe.
Expérience dans la traduction de la stratégie en feuilles de route réalisables, en structures de gouvernance, en mécanismes opérationnels et en résultats mesurables.
Solide sens des affaires et capacité à relier la transformation à la valeur pour la clientèle, à la croissance, aux marges, aux flux de trésorerie, à la productivité et aux capacités organisationnelles.
Excellentes aptitudes en communication auprès de la haute direction, en animation et en synthèse.
Capacité à remettre en question les pratiques établies de façon constructive et à évoluer dans l’ambiguïté avec rapidité et discernement.
Connaissance des modèles commerciaux internationaux, des environnements de gestion de la relation client (CRM) et de planification des ressources de l’entreprise (ERP), ainsi que des processus clients de bout en bout.
Une expérience dans un environnement industriel, manufacturier, électromécanique ou de technologies interentreprises (B2B) constitue un atout. Une certification reconnue en transformation, en gestion du changement, en Lean, en Six Sigma ou en gestion de programmes constitue un atout.
Maîtrise de l’anglais.

Pour en savoir plus sur nous

La division Moteurs NEMA d’ABB commercialise, conçoit et fabrique des moteurs électriques industriels Baldor-Reliance®, principalement en Amérique du Nord. La division mise sur la qualité, la fiabilité et l’efficacité afin d’offrir une gamme complète de moteurs NEMA sur le marché, couvrant la plupart des segments et des applications industriels.

Nous valorisons les personnes de tous horizons. Postulez dès aujourd’hui po

jobs.title: Chief Information Officer/Director, Digital Services
jobs.description:
Job Description

About Red Deer

Red Deer sits at the heart of Central Alberta along the QEII corridor, perfectly positioned between Calgary and Edmonton. With more than 100,000 residents and a regional reach of over 300,000, it’s a growing hub for business, services, and opportunity.

Here, big-city amenities meet small-city ease. Enjoy abundant parks and trails, vibrant arts and culture, excellent recreation and education, and a strong sense of community.

With easy access to lakes, outdoor adventures, and the mountains, plus a thriving economy and high quality of life, Red Deer is an inviting place to live, work, and grow.

About The City Of Red Deer Municipal Government

The City of Red Deer is a dynamic municipal organization with a $480M operating budget, a $60M capital program, and a workforce of nearly 1,700 employees. It is focused on growing with purpose by attracting talented, community-minded people who want to make a difference.

Guided by the vision “Our City, One Voice,” Red Deer is building a thriving, inclusive, and connected community, with priorities centered on a vibrant economy, community wellbeing, and strong engagement.

At its core, the City values its people, embracing diverse perspectives and fostering a culture of collaboration, innovation, and shared success.

Are you a visionary technology leader who can turn digital possibilities into meaningful organizational impact?

The City of Red Deer is seeking a dynamic and forward-thinking Chief Information Officer (CIO) / Director, Digital Services to help shape the future of technology and digital service delivery across our organization. This is an exciting opportunity to lead enterprise technology strategy, champion innovation and modernization, and build the secure, reliable digital foundations that support essential municipal services. If you thrive at the intersection of technology, people and organizational transformation, this is your opportunity to make a lasting impact on how we work, serve and grow.

The Opportunity

The City of Red Deer is seeking an accomplished and innovative technology executive to join our Corporate Performance and Supports Division as Chief Information Officer (CIO) / Director, Digital Services
.

Reporting to the Deputy Executive Director, Corporate Performance and Supports, the CIO will provide strategic and operational leadership for the City's enterprise technology environment, guiding digital modernization while ensuring the reliability, security and sustainability of the technology services that support municipal operations and community service delivery.

Leading a diverse team of approximately 50 professionals, the CIO will play a pivotal role in shaping the City's technology future, strengthening organizational capabilities and translating emerging digital opportunities into practical, sustainable solutions.

With responsibility for a broad enterprise portfolio, the successful candidate will provide leadership in six key areas:

Digital Strategy, Governance and Modernization: Shape and advance the City's enterprise technology strategy, architecture and roadmap. Champion innovation, automation and emerging technologies, including artificial intelligence, to enable organizational improvement and enhance municipal service delivery.
Technology Infrastructure, Cybersecurity and Resilience: Provide executive oversight of the City's technology infrastructure, cybersecurity and disaster recovery capabilities, ensuring critical systems and services remain secure, reliable and resilient in an increasingly complex digital environment.
Enterprise Solutions and Technology Delivery: Lead the planning, integration and modernization of enterprise applications and technology solutions, working collaboratively across departments to align investments with organizational priorities and deliver sustainable business value.
Technical Services and Customer Experience: Foster a service-oriented technology culture, strengthening technical support, operational performance and the employee experience through responsive, reliable and continuously improving digital services.
Enterprise Data Architecture and Integration: Advance the technical foundations that enable secure, connected and accessible organizational data, supporting effective integration, analytics and informed decision-making across the City.
People Leadership and Financial Stewardship: Inspire and develop a high-performing Digital Services team, strengthen leadership capacity and oversee significant technology investments, partnerships and service delivery models to ensure accountability, sustainability and value.

As the City's senior technology advisor, the CIO will work closely with executive leadership, departments and Council, as required, to navigate complex technology decisions, balance competing priorities and position the organization for long-term success.

The ideal candidate brings deep technical expertise, strong business acumen and a demonstrated ability to lead complex enterprise technology environments. They are a strategic thinker and accomplished people leader who understands the importance of operational excellence while embracing opportunities for innovation and transformation.

They bring sound judgment, exceptional communication and relationship-building skills, and the ability to translate complex technical considerations into clear, practical advice. Equally comfortable setting long-term direction and navigating immediate operational challenges, they inspire confidence, build collaborative partnerships and lead meaningful organizational change.

This is an exceptional opportunity for a technology leader who wants to do more than manage systems. It is an opportunity to shape digital direction, build organizational capability and help transform how municipal services are delivered for the community of Red Deer.

Required Qualifications

Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Information Technology, Information Systems, Computer Engineering or a related technical field. An equivalent combination of education and progressively responsible technology leadership experience may be considered.
10+ years of progressively responsible experience in Information Technology or Digital Services, including 5+ years in a technology leadership role with significant responsibility for enterprise technology services, teams and operations.
Experience developing and implementing organization-wide technology strategies, including infrastructure, enterprise applications, cybersecurity, data management and digital modernization.
Experience leading complex technology and data transformation initiatives and supporting teams through organizational change.
Experience managing significant operating and capital budgets, technology investments, vendor relationships and contracts.
Strong technical understanding of enterprise architecture, cloud technologies, cybersecurity, data governance and emerging technologies.
Ability to provide sound strategic and operational advice to senior leaders. Strong judgment and the ability to explain complex technology matters to non-technical audiences.
Experience leading collaborative, accountable teams, developing leaders and building strong working relationships across an organization.

Preferred Qualifications

Graduate education in a related field.
Professional certifications in enterprise architecture, cybersecurity, cloud technologies, data and analytics, artificial intelligence, technology service management or project management.
Senior technology leadership experience in a municipality, public-sector organization, utility or similarly complex organization.
Experience assessing different technology service delivery options, including internal services, managed services, cloud solutions and external partnerships.
Experience leading organization-wide digital modernization and introducing emerging technologies, including artificial intelligence.
Knowledge of municipal operations, public-sector accountability, privacy legislation and regulatory requirements.

What We Offer

In addition to the competitive wages, we offer an excellent benefit package, pension plans, spending accounts and professional development opportunities to support your career growth.

We are committed to a healthy, vibrant, and sustainable community. Our employees are the cornerstone of our organization and working with us will provide you with work-life balance, career growth and job stability.

The opportunity to work in an ever-growing environment and to work with a dedicated and passionate group of people.

Affiliation:
Exempt

Status:
Regular Full-time

Remuneration:
$75.63 to $94.53 per hour ($148,045 to $185,042 per annum)

Hours of Work:
75 hours biweekly; Monday to Friday, some evening and weekend work may be required when needed.

Additional Information:
Closing date is November 25, 2026, or until a suitable candidate has been found.

The City of Red Deer does not permit the use of unauthorized internet resources or Artificial Intelligence (AI) tools (for example, Copilot, ChatGPT or any other form of AI) during interviews or any supervised or timed assessments. Any violation may be investigated and result in serious consequences, including the rejection of your application.

We thank you for your application. Only those selected for an interview will be contacted.

About Us

We are a municipal government, eager to meet tomorrow's challenges. Our employees are the cornerstone of our organization. We are always seeking creative and skilled individuals with the ability and desire to lead in our dynamic workplace. Each of our employees brings diverse experiences and perspectives, as well as unique skills and talents to the job. Our diverse employee base ensures an environment where individual, team, and organizational successes are embraced and celebrated. We strive to ensure a supportive and respectful work environment for all. Employees are treated fairly and have equal opportunity within the organization to thrive and attain their highest potential. We welcome your application and look forward to discussing how The City of Red Deer can become your next career choice.

Job Description

Title:
Director, Finance (CSM)

Id:
21596

At Husky TechnologiesTM, our success is based on your success. Our ability to keep our customers in the lead is based on building the strongest team possible.

Husky TechnologiesTM has a strong foundation built on innovation, close customer relationships and a unique culture and values. We are dedicated to offering our customers the highest quality products and services and are looking for people with the inspiration and talent to develop with us as we pursue our ambitious growth strategy. We are a leader in developing state-of-the-art technology and it is this technology base that uniquely positions us to serve customers who seek differentiation through solutions that provide speed, flexibility and maximum productivity. This capability is at the core of our mission and competitive strategy.

Husky TechnologiesTM offers a wealth of opportunity for personal growth and development. Most importantly, Husky Technologies TM offers an opportunity to work with – and be challenged by – a team of great people. Our success is possible because of the creativity, intelligence and passion of our people around the world and their desire to lead change. At the same time, we are not afraid to expect a lot and strive for leadership in all of our key markets. We are a company taking on new challenges and for the right people this means exceptional career development opportunities, the chance to be part of a team that is the best in the world at what we do and the experience that comes from working in an environment that demands constant transformation and innovation.

Husky TechnologiesTM is an exciting company with tremendous potential. We have a great team and great expectations. If you are attracted to bold goals, believe in uncompromising honesty, support mutual respect, care about environmental responsibility, have a passion for excellence and a desire to make a positive contribution – then we want you to join the Husky TechnologiesTM team!

The Finance Director serves as a strategic business partner to the Leadership Team in support of Husky’s Global Service Business and Customer Success Management strategy. This role provides leadership for financial planning, forecasting, performance analysis, governance, and decision support to drive profitable growth, improve operational performance, and strengthen financial visibility across service revenue streams, including field service, contracts, parts, and other aftermarket offerings. The Finance Director is expected to influence strategic decisions, lead transformation initiatives, and build a high-performing finance capability that enables the business to scale effectively.

Key Responsibilities

Financial Planning & Forecasting

Lead the annual budget, quarterly forecast, and long-range planning processes for the service business.
Develop robust revenue, margin, cost, and headcount forecasts based on operational and commercial drivers.
Translate business strategies into financial plans with clear assumptions, risks, and opportunities.
Support scenario planning and sensitivity analysis for service growth, pricing, labor utilization, and investment decisions.

Performance Management & Analysis

Deliver timely and accurate monthly financial reporting and variance analysis for service revenue, gross margin, SG&A, and operating income.
Analyze business performance by region, product line, customer segment, channel, and service offering.
Monitor and explain key drivers of performance, including labor utilization, absorption, contract profitability, attach rates, response times, and service productivity.
Provide actionable insights and recommendations to improve growth, profitability, and working capital performance.

Business Partnering

Serve as the senior finance partner to service leadership, operations, commercial teams, and Customer Success leaders, providing insight and challenge on strategic priorities, business performance, and investment decisions.
Lead financial evaluation of pricing strategies, contract renewals, service program design, and capital or operating investments to support sustainable growth and margin expansion.
Provide proactive challenge and decision support to business leaders by identifying risks, opportunities, and trade-offs across growth, productivity, service delivery, and resource allocation.
Lead cross-functional evaluation of new service offerings, business models, and transformation initiatives that improve service coverage, utilization, fulfillment, cost efficiency, and customer value.
Sponsor finance and business transformation initiatives across Finance and Customer Success Management, including enhancements to processes, reporting, operating metrics, and decision frameworks that support growth, profitability, and scalability.

Management Reporting & KPI Development

Develop and enhance dashboards, reporting tools, and KPIs that improve transparency and decision-making.
Standardize definitions and reporting for critical service metrics across the organization.
Improve reporting automation and self-service analytics capabilities where possible.
Present clear financial results and business insights to senior leadership

Process Improvement & Governance

Strengthen forecasting accuracy, reporting discipline, and financial controls within the service business.
Drive continuous improvement in FP&A processes, planning models, and reporting frameworks.
Ensure alignment with corporate finance requirements, accounting policies, and internal controls
Support month-end close and planning processes in partnership with accounting and finance teams.

Qualifications

Bachelor’s degree in Finance, Accounting, Economics, or a related field required.
CPA, CMA, CFA, or MBA preferred.
10+ years of progressive experience in FP&A, finance business partnering, commercial finance, or operational finance, including leadership responsibility.
Experience in a service, aftermarket, field service, maintenance, or contract-based business strongly preferred.
Strong financial modeling, forecasting, and business analysis skills.
Advanced proficiency in Excel and experience with ERP and planning/reporting systems.
Executive presence with strong communication, presentation, and stakeholder management skills, and the ability to influence senior leaders across functions and regions.
Proven ability to work cross-functionally in a fast-paced, performance-driven environment

Preferred Experience In a Service Business

Understanding of service revenue models such as time and materials, service contracts, preventive maintenance, subscriptions, and parts/service bundles.
Experience analyzing operational KPIs such as technician utilization, service efficiency, contract margins, backlog, renewal rates, and service attach rates.
Familiarity with pricing strategy, labor productivity, installed base analytics, and customer lifecycle economics

Core Competencies

Strategic leadership
Financial and commercial acumen
Analytical rigor
Executive business partnership
Influence and executive communication
Problem solving
Process improvement
Results orientation and a bias for action

Team Development

Build and lead a high-performing finance team with strong capability in financial analysis, strategic thinking, business partnership, and change leadership.
Lead, coach, and develop team members, including succession planning, capability building, and development of future finance leaders.

Financial Leadership

Provide consistent, timely, accurate, and decision-oriented financial reporting for the service business, with greater automation and self-service access to insights where possible

Husky TechnologiesTM offers a competitive compensation and benefits package and excellent opportunities for growth and advancement. We are committed to equal employment opportunity and respect, value and welcome diversity in our workplace. Husky Technologies TM also values being a great place to work and strives to maintain a safe workplace. Accordingly, Husky TechnologiesTM conditions all offers of employment on satisfactory completion of background checks.

At UBC, we believe that attracting and sustaining a diverse workforce is key to the successful pursuit of excellence in research, innovation, and learning for all faculty, staff and students. Our commitment to employment equity helps achieve inclusion and fairness, brings rich diversity to UBC as a workplace, and creates the necessary conditions for a rewarding career.

Job Description Summary

The Director, Space Planning and Facilities Management is responsible for the overall strategic leadership of the planning, development, management and utilization of Faculty of Medicine Academic Space.

The Director, Space Planning & Facilities Management leads staff and external consultants, ensures appropriate space allocation and management policies and procedures are developed and implemented, space and facility plans are successfully executed to meet the changing needs of the Faculty, key partner’s relationships are built and maintained, and a culture of integrity, collegiality, and agility is fostered.

As most of the Faculty’s 1.8M square feet of Academic Space is built, owned, operated and/or maintained by other agencies and institutions under legislation, utilization agreements, or institutional regulations, the Director initiates, directs, and negotiates on behalf of the Faculty to ensure the Faculty’s space and facilities requirements are met.

Organizational Status

Reports directly to the Managing Director, Operations, Faculty of Medicine.

Leading a cross-functional team of professionals, the Director, Space Planning & Facilities Management provides strategic direction and planning for all aspects of Faculty of Medicine Academic Space to align Faculty goals, objectives, and strategies with those of the University and institutional partners.

With the high volume and complexity of the position requirements, it is important that the successful candidate have a team-oriented and flexible disposition and demonstrated leadership, problem-solving, and collaborative planning skills.

The Director’s primary work site is UBC Vancouver campus. The Director is required to travel to and work at various clinical campuses and academic sites across BC.

Work Performed

Strategic & Tactical Leadership

Represents the Faculty of Medicine’s s interest while interacting with Ministries, Health Authorities and University Leaders regarding academic facilities, capital project requirements, and other related academic space issues. Ensures Health Authority projects conform to Section 45 of the Hospital Act and Academic Space Protocol requirements.
Makes recommendations to Senior Leadership Team on strategic and policy matters related to the allocation, management and utilization of Academic Space, construction and renovation projects, and facility operations.
Resolves Academic Space disputes through negotiations and/or arbitration, developing innovative solutions and approaches to reconcile issues, ensuring that key partners’ relationships are built and maintained.
Forms, leads and participates in University and Health Authority committees and meetings, ensuring that appropriate consultative processes have been followed when developing policies, space and facility plans and reviews or when planning for new capital projects.
Provides strategic guidance and leadership to the Space Planning & Facilities Management Team, ensuring that resources and support are available to optimize performance and productivity within the unit.
Initiates and develops strategic and operational plans for the Space Planning & Facilities Management Team, creating tactics and action plans so that team goals can be achieved.
Provides leadership and direction for change management initiatives and risk management processes, with Health Authorities, University stakeholders, Faculty of Medicine key groups, consultants, contractors and other partners.
Oversees the general administration, project management, renovation and equipment budgets for Space Planning and Facilities Management unit , as required.
Develops projects, procedures, policies and other initiatives intended to maximize the allocation, management and utilization of Academic Space, reduce costs, or improve efficiency of space and facility operations.

Capital Projects Management

Leads short-term & long-term construction project planning for the Faculty of Medicine education programs, overseeing the compilation of requirements and specifications, evaluating and prioritizing options, coordinating funding requests, identifying and securing resources, obtaining financial and contractual approvals, establishing project goals, timelines and budgets.
Oversees capital projects at University and Health Authority facilities across BC, ensuring that functional program and technical requirements, as well as space and other related guidelines and policies as agreed are followed by University and/or Health Authority planners, contractors, architects and other parties, at times within a Public Private Partnership environment.
Ensures that the requirements and best interests of the Faculty of Medicine are realized in each project, integrating and coordinating with Academic Leaders of Clinical, Community, Research and Education, Department Heads and School Directors, AV/IT professionals and other consultants.
Forms, leads, and participates in project committees or working groups, ensuring that consultative processes have been followed and fostering relationships with key groups to enhance collaborations and partnerships.
Engages in the selection and activities of planners, architects, consultants, and contractors retained for planning, designing, construction, operations and maintenance of Faculty of Medicine facilities, consistent with appropriate University, Health Authority and Ministry policies.
Oversees the management of Ministry of Infrastructure minor capital l funding for Academic Space upgrades and renovations at Health Authorities sites.
Ensures all engineering life-cycle and maintenance standards for faculty assets are adhered to by University or Health Authority staff and external contractors, as appropriate.
Guides senior Academic Leaders in the design process for new and renovated teaching and learning facilities and the development of Academic Space allocation, management and booking policies.

Space Planning & Facility Management

Initiates and approves the creation and development of functional programs for Faculty of Medicine teaching and learning facilities across BC, and provides technical expertise and recommendations to the Managing Director, Operations, Faculty of Medicine. .
Leads short-term and long-term space and facility reviews of Departments, Research Centres/Institutes, Schools, Education programs and administrative units, , including moves and new acquisitions, negotiating and coordinating with Ministry, Health Authority, University, and key partners to secure spatial resources and approvals.
Provides direction and assistance to Department Heads, School Directors and Associate Deans in planning and allocating administrative and research space, ensuring compliance with Faculty space allocation & management policies and compatibility with the long-term objectives of the Faculty.
Participates in University and Health Authority space planning and facility management committees, such as the UBC Property & Planning Advisory Committee, UBC Learning Spaces, and other initiatives, including negotiations for leasing, acting in the best interests of the Faculty.
Ensures that all Faculty Academic Space is allocated and utilized equitably and efficiently, in accordance with Faculty, University and Health Authority guidelines, standards and policies, and as required in the Academic Space Protocols with Health Authorities

Academic Learning Spaces

Oversees the management of over 500+ Faculty of Medicine teaching and learning spaces including video-conference facilities, seminar rooms, lecture theatres, on-call rooms, lounges and other teaching facilities across the Province, ensuring that Faculty requirements are met, while promoting collaborative agreements with Health Authority and other University groups to attain optimal utilization of these spaces and resources.
Oversees the development of tools, systems and processes to ensure efficient and effective management of Academic Space, including the Faculty of Medicine Academic Space Inventory (through Archibus).
Leads the development of space policies, guidelines and processes for the Faculty of Medicine, incorporating national and international space standards for administrative, research and teaching facilities, and within the Health Authority and University contexts, to ensure equitable, efficient and collaborative allocation and utilization of Faculty resources.
Participates on the Faculty of Medicine Health & Safety Committee to ensures that health, safety & security concerns in Academic Space are addressed appropriately, and any deficiencies are actioned.

Consequence of Error/Judgement

The work Space Planning & Facilities Management unit is used in decision making, reporting, planning and provision of information to the University, Health Authorities, and Ministries. High level of decision -making is required. The position is required to exercise independent judgement in all areas of Space Planning & Facilities Management operation along with maturity, collegiality and initiative while developing relationships and partnerships.

Inappropriate actions or indiscretions in judgment can negatively impact the Faculty of Medicine reputation with internal and external partners and , have a detrimental effect on Faculty operations.

Supervision Received

The Director reports to the Managing Director, Operations, Faculty of Medicine, and works independently within the general policy guidelines to achieve overall objectives..

Supervision Given

Directly supervises the Senior Planner, Manager-Major Capital Projects, and three Facility Managers: Academic Learning Spaces, LSC Operations, and Administration & Research Space on the Space Planning & Facilities Management team.

Makes bi-weekly checks of work progress to ensure milestones are achieved. Position provides guidance to reporting staff on more strategic issues. Determines objectives, priorities, status and measures accomplishments against operational plan goals, objectives and performance standards.

The incumbent:

Establishes and maintains close and effective working relationships with the Ministries of Health Infrastructure, and Post-Secondary Education, Health Authority and University partners to ensure Academic Space functional requirements of the Faculty of Medicine are met. Works with all parties at policy, program, functional, implementation and management levels;
Advises Senior Faculty leadership, Departments, Schools, Research Institutes, Centres, and other key players (both faculty and staff) in the Faculty of Medicine;
Works closely with the Senior Education and Research Leaders, AV/IT professionals, and user groups in projects and other initiatives; and

At Husky TechnologiesTM, our success is based on your success. Our ability to keep our customers in the lead is based on building the strongest team possible.

Husky TechnologiesTM has a strong foundation built on innovation, close customer relationships and a unique culture and values. We are dedicated to offering our customers the highest quality products and services and are looking for people with the inspiration and talent to develop with us as we pursue our ambitious growth strategy. We are a leader in developing state-of-the-art technology and it is this technology base that uniquely positions us to serve customers who seek differentiation through solutions that provide speed, flexibility and maximum productivity. This capability is at the core of our mission and competitive strategy.

Husky TechnologiesTM offers a wealth of opportunity for personal growth and development. Most importantly, Husky Technologies TM offers an opportunity to work with – and be challenged by – a team of great people. Our success is possible because of the creativity, intelligence and passion of our people around the world and their desire to lead change. At the same time, we are not afraid to expect a lot and strive for leadership in all of our key markets. We are a company taking on new challenges and for the right people this means exceptional career development opportunities, the chance to be part of a team that is the best in the world at what we do and the experience that comes from working in an environment that demands constant transformation and innovation.

Husky TechnologiesTM is an exciting company with tremendous potential. We have a great team and great expectations. If you are attracted to bold goals, believe in uncompromising honesty, support mutual respect, care about environmental responsibility, have a passion for excellence and a desire to make a positive contribution – then we want you to join the Husky TechnologiesTM team!

The Finance Director serves as a strategic business partner to the Leadership Team in support of Husky’s Global Service Business and Customer Success Management strategy. This role provides leadership for financial planning, forecasting, performance analysis, governance, and decision support to drive profitable growth, improve operational performance, and strengthen financial visibility across service revenue streams, including field service, contracts, parts, and other aftermarket offerings. The Finance Director is expected to influence strategic decisions, lead transformation initiatives, and build a high-performing finance capability that enables the business to scale effectively.

Key Responsibilities

Financial Planning & Forecasting

Lead the annual budget, quarterly forecast, and long-range planning processes for the service business.
Develop robust revenue, margin, cost, and headcount forecasts based on operational and commercial drivers.
Translate business strategies into financial plans with clear assumptions, risks, and opportunities.
Support scenario planning and sensitivity analysis for service growth, pricing, labor utilization, and investment decisions.

Performance Management & Analysis

Deliver timely and accurate monthly financial reporting and variance analysis for service revenue, gross margin, SG&A, and operating income.
Analyze business performance by region, product line, customer segment, channel, and service offering.
Monitor and explain key drivers of performance, including labor utilization, absorption, contract profitability, attach rates, response times, and service productivity.
Provide actionable insights and recommendations to improve growth, profitability, and working capital performance.

Business Partnering

Serve as the senior finance partner to service leadership, operations, commercial teams, and Customer Success leaders, providing insight and challenge on strategic priorities, business performance, and investment decisions.
Lead financial evaluation of pricing strategies, contract renewals, service program design, and capital or operating investments to support sustainable growth and margin expansion.
Provide proactive challenge and decision support to business leaders by identifying risks, opportunities, and trade-offs across growth, productivity, service delivery, and resource allocation.
Lead cross-functional evaluation of new service offerings, business models, and transformation initiatives that improve service coverage, utilization, fulfillment, cost efficiency, and customer value.
Sponsor finance and business transformation initiatives across Finance and Customer Success Management, including enhancements to processes, reporting, operating metrics, and decision frameworks that support growth, profitability, and scalability.

Management Reporting & KPI Development

Develop and enhance dashboards, reporting tools, and KPIs that improve transparency and decision-making.
Standardize definitions and reporting for critical service metrics across the organization.
Improve reporting automation and self-service analytics capabilities where possible.
Present clear financial results and business insights to senior leadership

Process Improvement & Governance

Strengthen forecasting accuracy, reporting discipline, and financial controls within the service business.
Drive continuous improvement in FP&A processes, planning models, and reporting frameworks.
Ensure alignment with corporate finance requirements, accounting policies, and internal controls
Support month-end close and planning processes in partnership with accounting and finance teams.

Qualifications

Bachelor’s degree in Finance, Accounting, Economics, or a related field required.
CPA, CMA, CFA, or MBA preferred.
10+ years of progressive experience in FP&A, finance business partnering, commercial finance, or operational finance, including leadership responsibility.
Experience in a service, aftermarket, field service, maintenance, or contract-based business strongly preferred.
Strong financial modeling, forecasting, and business analysis skills.
Advanced proficiency in Excel and experience with ERP and planning/reporting systems.
Executive presence with strong communication, presentation, and stakeholder management skills, and the ability to influence senior leaders across functions and regions.
Proven ability to work cross-functionally in a fast-paced, performance-driven environment

Preferred Experience In a Service Business

Understanding of service revenue models such as time and materials, service contracts, preventive maintenance, subscriptions, and parts/service bundles.
Experience analyzing operational KPIs such as technician utilization, service efficiency, contract margins, backlog, renewal rates, and service attach rates.
Familiarity with pricing strategy, labor productivity, installed base analytics, and customer lifecycle economics

Core Competencies

Strategic leadership
Financial and commercial acumen
Analytical rigor
Executive business partnership
Influence and executive communication
Problem solving
Process improvement
Results orientation and a bias for action

Team Development

Build and lead a high-performing finance team with strong capability in financial analysis, strategic thinking, business partnership, and change leadership.
Lead, coach, and develop team members, including succession planning, capability building, and development of future finance leaders.

Financial Leadership

Provide consistent, timely, accurate, and decision-oriented financial reporting for the service business, with greater automation and self-service access to insights where possible
